correctness.rationale: The correct J=2 optimized source coefficient is 2^-2(2/3)=1/6; exact rational generating-function matching gives a cubic pole polynomial. For r<=4/5 a uniform Chebyshev bound proves every n>=3 weight positive and n<=2 direct; for 4/5<=r<=r_* Bernstein signs certify n<=30 except sixth and an analytic Chebyshev tail bound certifies n>=31. The sixth weight is exactly g(r)/46656 in normalized coordinates and supplies necessity through 15/16. For larger r, complex poles are strictly closer than the only real pole, and Pringsheim rules out nonnegative Taylor coefficients. The independent standard-library checker reruns 340 exact-rational finite certificates; infinity relies on the stated analytic arguments.

value.rationale: Positive memory kernels applied to nonnegative discrete forcing motivate nonnegative impulse weights. The exact finite step-size bound determines when this stronger positivity survives for an A-stable higher-accuracy scheme; it is an intrinsic method/kernel property and improves the BDF2 admissible normalized step by a factor 2r_* approximately 1.8664. The endpoint sixth-weight phenomenon and universal larger-step obstruction are nontrivial; no general PDE or arbitrary-kernel significance is asserted.
